title: What Changed In eBay's Story?
detail:
What Changed In eBay's Story?
Trefis Team

EBAY

AMZN
WMT
MELI
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Image from Pixabay

Investors are paying a premium for eBay (EBAY). The stock currently trades at 4.3 times its sales over the past twelve months, compared to 3.1 for the S&P 500. Justifying that valuation requires tracking a recent shift in corporate messaging. Back in April 2025, during the fiscal Q1 2025 call, management emphasized the uncertainty that tariffs and trade policy changes created for eBay's sellers and buyers. That rhetoric has faded. So what has management been talking up instead?

eBay Now Talks Up eBay Live And Depop

During the fiscal Q2 2026 call on August 5, 2026, management talked up eBay Live, which posted another record quarter. Gross merchandise volume on eBay Live, the value of goods sold through it, grew roughly eightfold, management said. Furthermore, management believes the platform is gaining share across all 7 markets where it operates.

Management also said eBay had completed its acquisition of Depop the week before. This deal broadens eBay's fashion portfolio and expands its reach, management noted. On the same call, management talked up using AI to change how people buy and sell on eBay.

Management no longer emphasizing trade policy marks a recent departure. As late as the fiscal Q1 2026 call on April 29, 2026, management described shipping as a major focus for the year amid an increasingly complex trade policy landscape.

Shifts like this test every retirement plan. If your advisor recently retired, it is a good moment for a free second opinion from our partner firm.

eBay's Sales Have Sped Up Over The Past Year

Financial performance has accelerated over the past year. eBay's revenue grew 14.8% in the April to June 2026 quarter, up from 6.1% in the same quarter a year earlier. The operating margin rose to 21.6% in that quarter, compared to 17.5% a year earlier, so operating profit grew faster than revenue.

Certain segments within the marketplace expanded faster than the broader business. Gross merchandise volume across eBay grew 14% from a year earlier in fiscal Q2 2026, excluding currency moves, management said. Meanwhile, consumer-to-consumer trade, recommerce (the resale of used goods), and the categories eBay has chosen to focus on each grew more than 20%.

Should eBay Holders Worry Less About Tariffs Now?

For a holder, the quieter tone is a modest positive. Management did not raise trade policy on the latest call, though it called the trade landscape increasingly complex as recently as April. Beyond the rhetoric, eBay's sales growth and operating margin were both higher in the latest quarter than a year earlier. Shareholders have benefited over the past year as well. The stock returned 32.5%, compared to 17.3% for the S&P 500.

title: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk Teases ‘X Shop’ After Amazon Shuts Out Grok Agents
detail:
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk Teases ‘X Shop’ After Amazon Shuts Out Grok Agents
Anan Ashraf
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:21 AM PDT 3 min read
AMZN
SPCX
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

"Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon," Musk said in a post on X.

Musk also said on Thursday that if Grok Bot makes an error with a purchase or leaks information, SpaceX will cover any losses.

SpaceX and Amazon are already competing in the low-Earth satellite broadband market.

SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk on Thursday floated the idea of launching a competitor to shopping giant Amazon.com (AMZN) after users reported that the e-commerce giant is blocking his firm's Grok Bot agents from placing orders on the site.

"Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon," Musk said in a post on X after a user highlighted the issue and suggested an 'X Shop.'

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Screenshot 2026-10-15 132115.png

SPCX stock is currently trading 3.5% lower, while AMZN is down 0.3%.

Musk's Same-Day Endorsement Of AI Transactions

The post comes on the heels of Musk highlighting Grok Bot's ability to handle purchases. Earlier on Thursday, Musk replied to an X user who noted the ease of booking a flight with the help of the bot, calling the process way simpler than navigating an airline website. Musk responded to the post to say that if Grok Bot makes an error with a purchase or leaks information, SpaceX will cover any losses. He further highlighted that such a circumstance has not happened yet.

Screenshot 2026-10-15 132022.png

Grok Bot consists of autonomous AI agents that can complete multi-step tasks like shopping, booking, and administrative work. It was released in early beta form in August and is currently available through certain Grok subscription plans such as SuperGrok Heavy.

Amazon, meanwhile, has been blocking AI agents from its shopping site. In September, the company blocked Meta's Muse agent over concerns about identification, terms of use, and account access. Grok agents are facing similar hurdles while attempting to shop on the site, as per X users.

Existing SpaceX, Amazon Competition

SpaceX and Amazon are already competing in the low-Earth satellite broadband market. SpaceX already has more than 11,000 Starlink satellites in orbit and provides satellite internet across more than 100 countries. Amazon is meanwhile building its own, smaller constellation called Leo, formerly Kuiper. Service is currently in beta and slated for broader availability later in 2026. Leo is still lagging Starlink by a significant margin in constellation strength and availability.

How Did SPCX And AMZN Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around AMZN and SPCX stayed within the 'bearish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed in 'normal' to 'bullish' territory.

title: What Would Flat Store Sales Do To Home Depot Stock?
detail:
What Would Flat Store Sales Do To Home Depot Stock?
Trefis Team
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 11:20 AM PDT 3 min read
HD
AMZN
WMT
COST
LOW
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors who own Home Depot (HD) worry that sales at existing stores will stop growing. That worry is hardly far-fetched. On August 18, the home improvement retailer reported that comparable sales, its measure for existing stores, rose 1.7% in the quarter, with just 1.3% growth in its U.S. stores. That same day, management reaffirmed its forecast for fiscal 2026, which puts comparable sales growth at 0% to 2%. A flat year sits at the bottom of that range. What would a flat year actually cost Home Depot?

What A Flat Year Would Cost Home Depot

Home Depot recorded $165 billion in sales during its last full fiscal year, which ended in February 2026. Applied to those sales, the 1% comparable growth at the middle of management's range is worth up to about $1.65 billion, which a flat year would forgo. A shortfall of that size would dent the year, but not the company.

Profit has faced even more pressure than sales. Although Home Depot saw sales grow 2.5% over the twelve months to August 2026, its operating income slipped anyway, dropping to $21.0 billion from $21.6 billion a year earlier. That slide occurred over the three prior quarters. The latest quarter proved firmer, with operating income rising to $6.84 billion from $6.56 billion a year earlier. Still, Home Depot's twelve-month operating margin of 12.4% is the lowest recorded at any quarter-end in ten years. The bottom of management's operating margin forecast for fiscal 2026, 12.4%, matches that low.

How Well Could Home Depot Absorb A Flat Year?

Home Depot's cash flow certainly has room to absorb a flat year. The company generated $15.1 billion of free cash flow over the twelve months to August, compared against $9.22 billion paid in dividends. During that period, the company bought back no shares.

Management also expects growth beyond the existing stores, and its plan includes new stores. The forecast for fiscal 2026 puts total sales up 2.5% to 4.5%, running ahead of the range for comparable sales. Separately, during its last full fiscal year, Home Depot's main segment slipped 0.7% to $152 billion, while the business it reports as Other nearly doubled to $12.7 billion.

Debt presents a weaker side: Home Depot owed $52.9 billion in debt at the start of August, plus $9.7 billion of operating lease liabilities, while carrying just $2.09 billion of cash. Even so, the company maintained an operating income that was 8.7 times its interest expense over the twelve months to August.

The stock is another vulnerability, as it has fallen harder than the market before. During the 2022 inflation shock, Home Depot stock fell 34%, compared to a 24% drop for the S&P 500.

title: Is Costco Stock Increasing Your Market Risk?
detail:
Is Costco Stock Increasing Your Market Risk?
Trefis Team
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:12 AM PDT 3 min read
COST
^GSPC
WMT
AMZN
TGT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Costco Wholesale (COST) is a $436 billion retailer. Anyone buying the stock likely already holds a portfolio built around the S&P 500. A share that sinks alongside the broader market only multiplies a bad day, while one charting its own course can cushion the blow. So when the market has a bad day, what does Costco do to your money?

Costco Edged Up On The Index's Average Down Day

Recently, Costco shares have managed to yield a slight gain on the market's average down day. Over the year to October 14, 2026, the S&P 500 lost 0.585% on its average down day. On those exact days, a $10,000 holding in Costco added about $3.68 in value.

Performance was actually more muted on the market's good days. On the average up day, the index gained 0.641%, and Costco added just $1.84 to that same holding. The stock barely tracked the wider market at all. Its beta, measuring how far a stock moves for each 1% move in the index, sat at -0.14 over the past year.

Costco is not a calm stock, though. Over the past year, its volatility, measuring how widely a price swings over twelve months, was 19.9%. That compares to 12.7% for the S&P 500. The retailer has not piled onto existing market risk, yet it still subjects investors to wider swings of its own.

If you have held Costco Wholesale for years, your biggest question may be taxes, not its day-to-day swings. See how a tax-aware transition works.

Could Costco Start Tracking The Index Again?

The underlying business remains steady, alongside a recent pickup in growth. Revenue grew 10.1% in the twelve months to August 2026, up from 8.2% growth a year earlier. Furthermore, Costco's twelve-month operating margin reached 3.9%. That is its highest at any fiscal quarter end in data going back to fiscal Q1 2017. Net sales for the retail month of September rose 13.0% from a year earlier.

The stock's relationship to the broader market remains far less settled. Over the past year, Costco's daily moves showed almost no link to the index at all, recording a correlation of -0.09, where zero indicates no connection. However, over the five years to October 14, 2026, that same measure stood at 0.51. That closer tie shows Costco's shares certainly have moved in line with the market before.

Did Costco's Bigger Moves Pay Off For Holders?

Costco holders earned more than index holders, though they captured about as much for each unit of swing. Over the five years from October 15, 2021, to October 14, 2026, Costco returned 18.0% a year with dividends included. By comparison, the S&P 500 returned 13.1% a year.

The five most valuable companies in the world are U.S. stocks Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), Apple, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon. And 16 of the world's top 20 most valuable companies are U.S. firms.

The sheer size of these companies makes the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC), Nasdaq-100, and index funds and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) linked to these benchmarks increasingly top-heavy. Meaning that just a handful of stocks and themes can drive performance, for better or worse.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Concentration is amplified for investors with dual exposure to these massive companies through ETFs and their individual holdings. The focused structure has paid off big time for U.S. investors -- as U.S. stocks have generally outperformed international stocks since the financial crisis of 2008.

However, some investors may be looking to diversify their portfolios by investing in leading international companies such as Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM), Samsung Electronics (OTC: SSNLF), SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY), and ASML (NASDAQ: ASML).

You won't find these stocks in S&P 500 index funds because they aren't U.S.-based. You also won't find them in many popular growth ETFs, like the Vanguard Morningstar Growth ETF, which is benchmarked to a U.S.-specific index called the Morningstar U.S. Large Cap Growth Index.

Investors looking for an ETF built around international stocks have come to the right place. Here's why the Vanguard Total International Stock ETF (NASDAQ: VXUS) may be worth a closer look in October.

Image source: Getty Images.
8,790 international stock holdings

The Vanguard Total International Stock ETF holds 8,790 stocks from around the world. Japan makes up 15.5% of the fund, followed by 8.7% of companies in Taiwan, 8.3% UK companies, 8.1% Canada, 7% China, 6.4% South Korea, 5% France, 5% Switzerland, 4.8% Gemmany 4.4%, India, 4.3% Australia, and 22.5% other.

So compared to the S&P 500, where a single stock like Nvidia makes up 8.1% of the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: VOO), entire countries have similar weights in the Total International Stock ETF.

The Total International Stock ETF is far more diversified. The world's largest semiconductor foundry operator -- Taiwan Semiconductor -- semiconductor designers and manufacturers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix -- and semiconductor equipment manufacturer ASML are the four largest holdings. But they account for only 8.7% of the ETF. Beyond that, each holding accounts for less than 1% of the fund because only three non-U.S. stocks (excluding Saudi Arabian Oil, which the ETF doesn't own) have market caps over $1 trillion. For comparison, the four largest holdings in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF make up 26.2% of the ETF.

title: 5 Growth Stocks With Home Run Potential
detail:
5 Growth Stocks With Home Run Potential
Rick Orford, The Motley Fool

NVDA

Explore stocks on Coinbase

All of the market's biggest names today started small. For example, Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) went public on May 15, 1997, at an IPO price of $18 per share, or about $0.075 split-adjusted. Four splits turned each share into 240, so $1,000 then would have bought about 55.6 shares, which today would have grown into roughly 13,344 shares worth a total of about $3.45 million.

Obviously, that made Amazon a rare outlier. But if you're looking for small companies today that have some potential to follow a similar path, I recommend taking a look at Rocket Lab (NASDAQ: RKLB), IonQ (NYSE: IONQ), Oklo (NYSE: OKLO), Archer Aviation (NYSE: ACHR), and AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ: ASTS).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
Rocket Lab runs a full-service space business

Rocket Lab is the most established of the five. Its Electron rocket serves the small-satellite market, while its spacecraft, satellite components, and space systems business provides a broader growth engine. The company's strengths lie in the large size of the market it serves, and in its technological edge, especially in aerospace and defense.

That said, its main challenge is funding the scaling up of capital-intensive programs like its new medium-lift Neutron rocket, which it hopes to test fly for the first time next year.

Today, it has roughly $2.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents on its books, but it used $134.4 million in operating cash in the first half of 2026, while its share count rose about 10%. Meanwhile, it trades at a price-to-sales ratio of about 67. The bull case weakens if Neutron stalls or fails to drive massive revenue growth.

IonQ is powering the future of quantum computing

IonQ is chasing a different frontier: quantum computing. The company is developing a trapped-ion qubit system that has potential use cases across a wide range of industries, from materials science and drug discovery to logistics and cybersecurity. Its opportunity rests on market size and technology.

IonQ has yet to prove it can deliver a product that is broadly commercializable, let alone do so at scale, and that could make or break the bull case. The company reported a $608.8 million operating loss for the first half of 2026 and used $254.8 million in operating cash.

It holds nearly $3 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and available-for-sale securities. That said, thanks to its secondary stock sales, its share count has climbed about 72% since the end of 2024, and more equity financing could further dilute investors.
